Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Marco and I are excited about Redwood's routing and fallback story. We're starting to map out committed traffic if we go ahead with the annual Dedicated contract. Early ask below so you can start sketching a proposal.

Quick summary of expected workload (next 12 months):
- US (primary): steady-state 1.2k QPS, peak 2.8k QPS during business hours; average request size ~220 tokens upstream, model is a mix of 13B and 70B fine-tuned variants.
- EU (secondary): steady-state 300 QPS, peaks to 700 QPS; strict data residency requirement.
- APAC (pilot): 120 QPS initially, targeting 600 QPS by Q4.

SLOs: 95th percentile generation latency under 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and 500ms for longer prompts.

Can you confirm what a recommended regional pool layout would look like (A100 vs H100 mixes), an estimate of reserved capacity we'd need to commit to meet peak+buffer, and what fallback model variants you'd propose to avoid regional overprovisioning? Also attaching our rough QPS spreadsheet.

Appreciate a quick sketch before our procurement meeting next Wednesday.

Best,
Aisha
VP Product, BrightLayer AI

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 08:32 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aisha — thanks for the clear numbers and the spreadsheet. Looping in Vivek (sales lead) and Karthik (solutions) to propose a regional sketch. We'll put a conservative buffer for burst plus a recommended canary fallback path to lower-cost quantized variants.

Attaching a first-pass sizing rationale (summary below). I'm keeping assumptions explicit so procurement can map commits to unit economics.

Assumptions:
- Latency SLO will be met for 95th perc when model is served on H100 for 70B and A100 for 13B.
- Average token generation per request ~ 150 tokens for tail latency calc.
- We assume continuous batching efficiency: effective throughput per GPU improves by ~1.8x at QPS > 500 with batching and KV cache reuse.
- Canary fallback: 70B FP16 -> 70B 4-bit quant variant (lower cost, slightly higher latency under load); 13B can be served on cheaper vRAM-optimized A100 variants.

Recommended regional pools (initial reserved capacity):
- US (primary): 14 H100s + 22 A100s (equivalent to ~36 production units). Rationale: H100s to handle 70B inference at peak; A100s for 13B and non-critical workloads. This supports steady-state + 1.5x burst buffer with batching.
- EU (regional): 4 H100s + 6 A100s (data residency, smaller pool but pinned to EU region).
- APAC (pilot): 2 H100s + 4 A100s; grow to 6 H100s + 8 A100s if QPS trend by Q4 reaches targets.

Cost estimate (monthly committed spend): a preliminary ballpark (will refine with pricing ops): US ~$280k/mo, EU ~$70k/mo, APAC ~$35k/mo; blended committed discount tiers apply.

Caveats & risks:
- If BrightLayer requires strict single-tenant HSM/KMS in APAC region, we may need additional lead time for Private deployment.
- Model weights >70B with long contexts materially increase H100 counts; need exact model sizes and concurrency targets per endpoint.

I'll convert this to a short PDF with charts. Tessa/Vivek — flag any commercial constraints you want modeled in the MAP.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team — quick commercial notes before we hand to procurement:

1) Commit tiers: We should propose a two-tier commitment: Core reserved capacity (committed GPUs) and burst bucket (pay-as-you-go up to X% over commit at elevated rate). Suggest core = 80% of our recommended reserved counts; burst capacity handles transient peaks. This reduces upfront spend for BrightLayer but keeps us protected.

2) SLA & credits: Recommend standard Dedicated SLA with an enhanced latency SLO addendum for US region only (BrightLayer asked for tighter latencies on primary traffic).

3) Marketplace/Procurement: Danielle from the cloud partner is looped for regional capacity placement options and potential cost offsets via marketplace credits.

Tessa — can you draft the MAP milestones (signatures, SOC2 evidence, enterprise onboarding window)? Laura — please watch for contract redlines on data residency and KMS requirements.

— Vivek
